title: Most Reformed: some falls add new eternal-death guilt until repentance; lighter faults do not
source_text: LXI. Quin ostendimus Reformatos, saltem plerosque, aperte docere quaedam esse peccata, in quae fidelis incurrens novo mortis aeternae reatu actu involvitur, & ineptus redditur qui ingrediatur in regnum coelorum, donec per poenitentiam iis renun-tiarit, & ab iis reipsa & in totum abstinuerit: ita ut si mors illum deprehenderet in ejusmodi peccato, verbi causa latrocinantem atque adulterantem, & vitae proximi sui insidiantem, minime servari posset, & vitae ac gloriae coelestis particeps fieri: alia vero peccata novum mortis aeternae reatum non inducere, nec hominem ineptum red-dere qui admittatur in regnum coelorum, etiamsi mors illum in aliquo hujusmodi peccato deprehendat. Cujusmodi sunt ex eorum mente peccata quaedam leviora, ut cogitatio frivola, risus immodicus, verbum otiosum, & defectus bonis operibus fide-lium adhaerentes, & ratione quorum a perfectione summa, quam legis rigor exigit, deficiunt.
pass_a_gloss: Nay we have shown that the Reformed, at least most of them, openly teach that there are certain sins into which a faithful person running is actually involved in a new guilt of eternal death, and is rendered unfit to enter the kingdom of heaven, until by repentance he has renounced them and in reality and wholly abstained from them: so that if death should overtake him in a sin of that sort—for example thieving and committing adultery and lying in wait for his neighbor’s life—he could by no means be saved and made partaker of heavenly life and glory: but that other sins do not induce a new guilt of eternal death, nor render a man unfit to be admitted into the kingdom of heaven, even if death overtake him in some sin of that sort. Of which kind in their mind are certain lighter sins, as a frivolous thought, immoderate laughter, an idle word, and defects clinging to the faithful’s good works, by reason of which they fall short of the highest perfection which the law’s rigor exacts.
pass_b_english: Most Reformed: capital falls add new death-guilt and bar heaven until real repentance—death mid-crime would damn.
Lighter thoughts, laughter, idle words, and work-blemishes add no such new guilt even if death finds them.

choices.english: could by no means be saved
choices.why: Death in unrepened capital sin ≠ salvation.
